selection.reviewer_identity: claude-opus-5-5 storyboard-critic, isolated phone leaf, round 17
selection.reason: Both films share the same opening (s1), street flood (s4), count grid, close lane shot with the may highlight, stamp passage and close (s9). Where they differ, A's ground-level pictures make the mechanism easier to read. In s6 (28.4 to 32.6 s) A tracks the car at road level: its red brake lamp is clearly visible 30.6 to 31.4 s, the background scroll slows, and the pale water patch is in view at road level before the cut. In s3 (13.2 to 17.4 s) A shows rain, a limestone bank and the car in the current from the first frame. The round 15 highlight fix holds in both: amber lands on may in the quote card's first line at 34.2 s, as the front wheel meets the water at 34.0 s.
selection.rejected_reason: B's overhead passages trade legibility for variety. In s6-shot1 (29.2 to 32.6 s) the quote card covers most of the standing water, the slowing cue is a few red pixels at 30.8 to 32.4 s, and the caption covers much of the car at 28.6 s. Its overhead creek (13.2 to 15.2 s) is a near-static car in a channel with no rain drawn. The B s1 and s4 replacements now match A's ground-level shots exactly.

a.reviewer_identity: claude-opus-5-5 storyboard-critic, isolated phone leaf, round 17
a.reviewed_at: 2026-10-20 (exact clock time not available to this leaf)
a.basis: Chronological film-decoded phone images, 5 samples per second plus the final frame. No MP4 playback and no listening. Motion between samples is inferred only from consecutive frames, and anything not visible stays unresolved.

strongest_frame.observed: Close side view: the white roof-pod car's front wheel is in pale standing water with ripples at the tire, and the quote card above carries an amber highlight on may. The whole mechanism reads in one picture.

weakest_frame.observed: 13.2 to 15.2 s: wide creek with the car about one sixth of frame width, sitting nearly still. At 15.4 to 17.4 s the car tilts nose-up and travels right with a bow wave ahead of it. It moves along its own heading, so the narrated swept sideways by the current reads more like fording. Non-blocking: the car is plainly empty, in brown flood water, and disclosed as the April 20th account.

notes: s1 to s2 (6.8 to 7.0 s): the board's visible bridge, a car pin riding from the curb onto the map, does not appear. The map opens with its pins already placed. Non-blocking.
s7 (39.2 to 40.8 s): two blue-sleeved forearms, holding a pen and a stamp, both enter from the right edge with no body visible. They read as one off-frame clerk's two hands. Non-blocking finish note.
s8 (43.0 to 45.6 s): the only change is the weather tag rocking on its wire, about 3 s and under the 4 s interval. This is the film's thinnest information interval.

s9 (52.8 to 54.6 s): the record card first appears lying flat on the asphalt in front of the car and then grows toward the camera. It works as an editorial juxtaposition, not a supported object, and it resolves into the readable split at 56.4 s.
The caption band sits about two thirds down the frame and overlaps the lower water and wake at 31.0 to 31.8 s and 35.0 to 36.4 s. The principal contact stays visible above it.

subject_recognition.observed: The white roof-pod SUV is recognizable in every car scene: curb, cabin, creek, street, lane and lot. The record card text reads at phone size: Federal recall record, Software, 3,791, The remedy is currently under development. The airport cue (airplane and car sign) is present at 0 to 6.8 s and 50 to 58.4 s.

contact_and_consequence.observed: Each contact leaves a completed result. The stamp is pressed and lifts to reveal the Software recall mark (26.0 to 27.6 s). The front wheel meets the water at 34.0 s and the wake persists to 36.8 s. The stamp reveals Under development (40.0 to 40.8 s). Check badges land on each car left to right (46.0 to 47.0 s).

surface_finish.observed: The flat vector finish is consistent. The car has rims, roof pod, dark glazing, a mud band in s3 and reflections in water. The cards have soft shadows. The quote card is legible. Finish is adequate for the chosen style. Native-scale detail was not inspected at this scope.

closing_payoff.observed: The film returns to the airport curb with the car's rear door opening (51.2 s). The record card's remedy row and Under development stamp then grow beside it and hold as a split with an underline (56.4 to 58.4 s). This answers the opening question without inventing an outcome.

first_frame.observed: At 0.0 s the airport curb, the Ride requested phone card and the airplane sign are in frame. The car glides in from the left and is at the bay by 1.0 s.

visual_progression.observed: Curb ride, then map outline closing, then creek, then stranded street car, then record filling, then lane mechanism, then remedy stamp, then interim checks, then curb beside the record. Each scene changes state on screen.

shot_variety.observed: Framings: wide curb, interior cabin detail, close phone, medium and close tabletop map, wide and closer creek, wide and close street, desk and close grid, tracked wide road, close side wheel, close card, lot, wide and medium curb, split.

performed_turn.observed: The car decelerates with its brake lamp lit (30.6 to 31.4 s) and stops short of the water in the wide shot. In the close shot it rolls into the water at 34.0 s and leaves a wake, while may lights at 34.2 s. No stop is drawn.

pace.observed: First change happens within 0.8 s. No observed interval longer than 4 s lacks a change. The thinnest stretches are 4.0 to 5.2 s (cabin hold) and 43.0 to 45.6 s (tag rocking).

closing_answer.observed: Open-door airport car with the Under development record beside it, held as a split with an underline. This matches the board's closing answer.

finished_art.observed: The finished vector world is consistent across scenes. Minor notes: two right-side forearms in s7, the floating card on asphalt at 52.8 s, and a small creek car at 13.2 to 14.4 s.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: A driverless car picks up at the San Antonio airport curb. Two disclosed April examples show empty cars in a creek and stranded in a flooded street. The federal record counts 3,791 cars. An illustrated car slows and then rolls into standing water as the recall sentence's may lights. The remedy is stamped under development, the interim checks reach every car by April 20, and the close sets the open ride beside the unfinished remedy.
story_review.opening_to_ending: It opens on the question of who can now hail a driverless ride to the airport, and closes on the same curb with its door open beside a record whose remedy is under development. This answers the question without inventing a fix or an outcome.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2 to s3 at 13.0 to 13.2 s: from a tabletop map to a wide creek whose small car is nearly still for its first second. The bridge is only the disclosure label change; it is honest but visually abrupt.
